land.text: Saurashtra and Gujarat: Bhatarka was 'a military governor of Saurashtra under Gupta Empire' and 'had established himself as the independent around 475 CE'

predecessors.note: The Gupta dossier records the matching loss at 476; all but two cells of Cliopatria's 476 Maitraka shape lie in the Gupta shape of 475.

land.text: Gujarat and Saurashtra, where Cliopatria's Gurjara-Pratihara shape of 776 covers 603 of the 637 cells of the Maitraka core

successors.note: Page-silent: the Maitraka page names no successor and says only that the kingdom 'had weakened considerably' after 'repeated attacks by Arabs from the sea'; the transfer is Cliopatria's, which hands Gujarat to the Gurjara-Pratihara from 732, 44 years before the dynasty's end.

land.text: the Surat and Bharuch edge of southern Gujarat (32 cells)

capitals.name: Vallabhi (Valabhi, near Bhavnagar)
capitals.note: 'The Maitrakas ruled from their capital at Vallabhi' (Maitraka page); the Vallabhi page places it near Bhavnagar in Saurashtra. Neither page gives coordinates; they are the modern site (Vala).

rulers.name: Senapati Bhatarka
rulers.note: The list says c. 470 to c. 492; the state is drawn from 475. Reign years are the Vallabhi page's list, which the Maitraka page does not give; shared boundary years were moved to the earlier reign's end.

rulers.name: Dharasena IV (Ghana Sen IV)
rulers.note: Chakravarti Raja; the prose says he 'assumed the imperial titles of Paramabhattaraka Mahrajadhiraja Parameshvara Chakravartin'.

rulers.name: Siladitya II
rulers.note: The list has no ruler for 685-689.

correction.text: Saurashtra, where Bhatarka, 'a military governor of Saurashtra under Gupta Empire', 'had established himself as the independent around 475 CE'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the founding year, Saurashtra alone (ledger /0; infobox 'Founded: 475'). Cliopatria's row begins in 476, when its shape adds the rest of Gujarat (ledger /1).

144,789 km2 for 476-533, Gujarat from Kutch to the Gulf of Khambhat (604 of its 617 cells lie in Gujarat, 287 in Saurashtra). 615 of the 617 cells lie in the Gupta shape of 475, matching the Gupta dossier's loss at 476. The page gives no area; it says only that Bhatarka 'had established himself as the independent around 475 CE' (infobox 'Founded: 475'), a year before Cliopatria's row, so Saurashtra alone holds in 475 (new keyframe maitraka-dynasty_475) and the full 476 shape holds 476-533 as Cliopatria draws it (ledger /1 adds Gujarat outside Saurashtra in 476). It also says 'During the reign of the next ruler, Dharasena III, north Gujarat was included in this kingdom' (Dharasena III reigned 626-640 on the Vallabhi list), which suggests the early shape is too large in the north; no area is subtracted because the page gives no boundary. Toramana's Sanjeli inscription claims 'conquest and control over Malwa and Gujarat' (Toramana page, undated, defeated in 515); neither the Maitraka nor the Toramana page links the two, so no Hun occupation is drawn.
145,067 km2 for 534-554; two cells (69.3-69.4 E, 22.8-22.9 N) are added to the 476 shape and no page explains them. Unverified: page budget.

149,998 km2 for 555-611: 60 cells are added in the south-east (69.2-74.7 E, 20.9-24.0 N), 39 of them inside the last Vakataka shape of 554. The Maitraka page dates no expansion for the reigns of Dhruvasena I to Dharasena II (the Vallabhi list: 520-595); kept as drawn. Unverified: page budget.

correction.text: unchanged shape, holding 612-615 (a change of years)

keyframe_review.note: 150,557 km2 for 612-646 (three cells more than the 555 shape). The 'Virdi copperplate grant (616 CE) of Kharagraha I proves that his territories included Ujjain': the shape holds 612-615 and the new keyframe below adds Ujjain from 616.

New keyframe: Kharagraha I's Virdi grant of 616 places Ujjain in his territories ('proves that his territories included Ujjain'). The page gives no radius; 100 km around Ujjain is the researcher's reading of 'territories included Ujjain'. The page also says the Maitrakas 'came under the rule of Harsa in the mid-7th century, but retained local autonomy': a vassal relation, recorded in the ledger from 640 to 647 with counterpart harsha-s-empire (Cliopatria's Harsha's Empire shape also covers the whole Ujjain circle in 612-646, so harsha-s-empire should not draw Ujjain directly while the Maitrakas hold it). Harsha's southern boundary was the Narmada ('his realm covered much of northern and northwestern India, with the Narmada River as its southern boundary', Harsha page).
149,998 km2 for 647-655, the 555 shape again (three cells less than the 612 shape). Ujjain stays: no page ends the Maitraka hold on it before the 8th century.

correction.text: the 647 shape (Saurashtra and Gujarat) with Ujjain, 656-723; the added Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh cells are removed

keyframe_review.note: 303,531 km2 for 656-723, double the 647 shape: it adds 634 cells over Rajasthan (357 cells in all) and Madhya Pradesh (293) to 27.1 N and 77.8 E, 472 of them inside Cliopatria's own Gurjara-Pratihara shape of 732 and none in Harsha's Empire of 655. None of the five pages places the Maitrakas in Rajasthan or central Madhya Pradesh: the Maitraka page gives Saurashtra, north Gujarat and Ujjain, the Caliphate page has the Maitraka suzerain at Vallabhi ruling Nandipuri in southern Gujarat in 736, and Nagabhata (the Gurjara-Pratihara founder) at Ujjain c. 725. The 647 shape with Ujjain is used instead. Area check: no infobox area on any page. Repair pass: Ujjain stays in the shape through 731 (ledger: the loss is at 732).

correction.text: the 647 shape (Saurashtra and Gujarat) with Ujjain, 724-731; the added Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh cells are removed, as in the 656 keyframe

keyframe_review.note: 303,531 km2 for 724-731, the 656 shape unchanged; corrected as the 656 shape was. Cliopatria ends the row in 731 but the Maitraka kingdom lasts to 776 (infobox 'Dissolution: 776'; text 'ended by 783 CE'; the Vallabhi list ends with Siladitya VI, 762-776). Ujjain stays to 731: Junayd's force 'made incursions into its country (Avanti)' but 'Ujjain itself was not conquered' (Caliphate page), and no page dates its loss (see ledger, 732). The next keyframe carries Gujarat and Saurashtra alone for 732-776.

correction.text: Saurashtra and Gujarat without Ujjain and without the Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh cells, holding 732-776 (Cliopatria has no Maitraka shape after 731)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Ujjain goes to the Gurjara-Pratihara in 732 (ledger, confidence 1; Nagabhata I r. 730-760 'spread to Avanti at Ujjain'; Cliopatria's Gurjara-Pratihara row starts in 732) and the Maitraka core holds to 776 (infobox 'Dissolution: 776'; 'ended by 783 CE'). The Gurjara-Pratihara dossier should not draw Gujarat before 776 (their Cliopatria shape of 776 covers 603 of the Maitraka core's 637 cells).

region.text: Saurashtra, where Bhatarka was military governor under the Guptas

ledger.note: 475: Bhatarka makes himself independent in Saurashtra. 'Maitraka dynasty was founded by Senapati (general) Bhatarka, who was a military governor of Saurashtra under Gupta Empire' and 'had established himself as the independent around 475 CE'; infobox 'Founded: 475'; 'The Maitrakas ruled from their capital at Vallabhi.'

region.text: Gujarat outside Saurashtra: Kutch, north and south Gujarat in the 476 shape

ledger.note: 476: the rest of Gujarat joins the new Maitraka state. Cliopatria's 476 shape lies inside the Gupta shape of 475; the page says Maitraka rise is linked to 'the decline of the Gupta Empire' and names only Saurashtra, so the land outside Saurashtra is Cliopatria's reading. The Gupta dossier records the matching loss at 476.

region.text: the south-east edge (Narmada and Tapi side) added in 555 within the Vakataka shape

ledger.note: 555: the south-east of the Maitraka shape grows. Cliopatria's 555 shape adds 60 cells (39 in the last Vakataka shape of 554, 72.9-74.7 E, 20.9-23.6 N); the Maitraka page dates nothing between Dhruvasena I and Dharasena II. Counterpart (repair pass): the vakataka-kingdom dossier ends the Vakataka state in 510 and hands 'the northern Vakataka lands (Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, the Gujarat edge)' to kalachuris-of-mahishmati, so that is the holder named for the 39 cells; no page names who held this edge in 554, and Cliopatria still draws it in a Vakataka shape. Confidence 1; kalachuris-of-mahishmati has no dossier yet (listed by sa-02-d).

region.text: the north-east edge added in 555 outside the Vakataka shape

ledger.note: 555: the rest of the added edge belongs to no Cliopatria state. 21 of the 60 cells added in 555 lie outside any neighbouring shape.

region.text: Ujjain, in the territories of Kharagraha I

ledger.note: 616: Kharagraha I holds Ujjain. 'Virdi copperplate grant (616 CE) of Kharagraha I proves that his territories included Ujjain.' The grant shows the hold by 616, not the year of conquest, and the page names no former owner. Repair pass: Cliopatria's Harsha's Empire shapes of 612-646 cover the whole Ujjain circle (134 of 134 cells in 616, 133 in 640, none in the 647-655 shape), so Cliopatria's Harsha row and the keyframe below draw the same land in 616-646; the grant shows Maitraka possession of Ujjain in 616, so the harsha-s-empire dossier (sa-03) should not draw Ujjain directly while the Maitrakas hold it (a Harsha vassal from 640: see below).

region.text: the Maitraka state (Gujarat and Saurashtra with Ujjain) that 'came under the rule of Harsa'

ledger.note: c. 640: the Maitrakas come under Harsha. 'They came under the rule of Harṣa of Vardhana dynasty in the mid-seventh century' but 'retained local autonomy'; Dhruvasena II 'married the daughter of Harṣavardhana'. The page gives only 'mid-seventh century', so 640, Dhruvasena II's accession on the Vallabhi list (640-644), is bridged (confidence 1); Harsha reigned 606-647 (Harsha page, which does not mention the Maitrakas). The tint covers the drawn state (the 612 shape with Ujjain, which Cliopatria's Harsha's Empire shape also covers in 612-646). Maitraka is the vassal and harsha-s-empire the suzerain: the harsha-s-empire dossier (sa-03) should hold the mirror vassal_start with counterpart maitraka-dynasty.

region.text: the Maitraka state, which 'regained their independence after Harṣa's death'

ledger.note: 647: the Maitrakas regain their independence on Harsha's death. Maitraka page: they 'regained their independence after Harṣa's death'; Harsha page: 'Reign: April 606 – 647', 'Died: 647'. Cliopatria's Harsha's Empire shrinks from 965,211 km2 to 161,252 km2 in 647 and no longer holds Ujjain or Gujarat. The year rests on the Harsha page's death year; the Maitraka page gives no year. Mirror: harsha-s-empire vassal_end with counterpart maitraka-dynasty.

region.text: Gujarat and Saurashtra: 'conquered Gujarat' (Junayd), Saurashtra and the Gurjara kingdom of Nandipuri (Navsari grant)

ledger.note: 723: the Arab governor of Sindh, Junayd, raids Gujarat. 'Junayd ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Murri (723-726) recaptured Sindh, conquered Gujarat and parts of Rajasthan'; later raids by al-Hakam (731-740) reach 'Kacchella, Saindhava, Saurashtra, Cavotaka, Maurya and Gurjara'. The Caliphate page does not name the Maitrakas except as the 'King of Vallabhi'.

region.text: Ujjain, where the Gurjara-Pratihara founder Nagabhata I (r. 730-760) 'spread to Avanti at Ujjain'

ledger.note: 732: Ujjain passes to the Gurjara-Pratihara. The Caliphate page dates the defeat of 'a powerful army of Valacha Mlecchas' by Nagabhata to 'around 725 CE' (Gwalior inscription) but says 'there is no authentic information about where precisely he encountered them', that 'many historians believe that Nagabhata repulsed Arab forces at Ujjain', that Nagabhata I (r. 730-760) belonged to a dynasty 'believed to have started from the Jalore-Bhinmal area and spread to Avanti at Ujjain', and that 'Ujjain itself was not conquered' by Junayd's force. It dates neither the Pratihara hold of Ujjain nor the Maitraka loss. Moved from 724 in the repair pass: the c. 725 date belongs to the Valacha victory, not to Ujjain, and 732 meets Cliopatria's Gurjara-Pratihara row (it starts in 732 and holds 68 of the 134 Ujjain cells) and the page's reign start of Nagabhata I (730). Confidence 1: who held Ujjain before, and the year, are bridged.

region.text: Nandipuri in southern Gujarat, overrun by the Arabs as far as Navsari

ledger.note: 736: a Gurjara king of southern Gujarat is a vassal of Vallabhi. 'Jayabhata IV, Lord of Nandipuri, recorded in an inscription dated to 736 CE that he went to the aid of his suzerain, the King of Vallabhi'; the Arabs then overran his territory as far as Navsari. The inscription shows the relation in 736; its start is not on the page.

region.text: Gujarat and Saurashtra, after the defeat at Navsari (739) and al-Hakam's death (740)

ledger.note: 743: the Arabs have lost Gujarat. 'The Arabs lost their conquests in Rajasthan and Gujarat by 743'; they were 'decisively defeated at Navsari in 739 by Avanijanashraya Pulakeshin, a general of Vikramaditya II' and al-Hakam 'died in battle in 740 CE while fighting the Meds of north Saurashtra'.

776: the Maitraka line ends and with it the suzerainty over Nandipuri. No page dates the end of the Nandipuri relation; the Vallabhi list closes with Siladitya VI (762-776) and says Maitraka rule 'is believed to have ended during the second or third quarter of the eighth century when the Arabs invaded'.

region.text: Saurashtra and Gujarat, the Maitraka core

ledger.note: 776: the Maitraka kingdom ends at Vallabhi. Infobox 'Dissolution: 776'; 'The dynasty ended by 783 CE'; the kingdom 'had weakened considerably' after 'repeated attacks by Arabs from the sea'. The Vallabhi list closes with Siladitya VI (762-776). Cliopatria ends the row in 731. The page names no successor; Cliopatria gives Gujarat to the Gurjara-Pratihara.

wars.name: Arab campaigns in Gujarat (Junayd and al-Hakam)
wars.outcome: Junayd (723-726) 'conquered Gujarat and parts of Rajasthan' but 'forces invaded Malwa and achieved victory' while Ujjain was not taken; his gains were lost under Tamim (726); al-Hakam (731-740) campaigned into Gujarat, overran Nandipuri (736) and was defeated at Navsari in 739 by Avanijanashraya Pulakeshin and killed in 740 by the Meds of north Saurashtra; 'The Arabs lost their conquests in Rajasthan and Gujarat by 743'.
wars.note: The Caliphate page names the Maitrakas only as the suzerain 'King of Vallabhi'; the Maitraka and Vallabhi pages give the Arab invasion as the cause of the end of the line, in the second or third quarter of the eighth century or by 783, decades after these raids. The span is the years of the campaigns the page dates (723-743).

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary for the Maitrakas; the shape is an approximate Gujarat and Saurashtra block with Ujjain from 616.

notes: Page budget up to 5 pages, all used (the Dhruvasena II page would not load: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhruvasena_II). THE SHAPE: no page gives an area. Cliopatria's 656-731 shape (303,531 km2) doubles the earlier core with 634 cells of Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh that no page gives the Maitrakas and that overlap Cliopatria's own Gurjara-Pratihara shape of 732 by 472 cells; it is corrected to the Gujarat core plus Ujjain (verdict adjust). Cliopatria also ends the row in 731, 45 years before the pages' 776 (infobox) or 783 (text); the Gurjara-Pratihara dossier should not draw Gujarat before 776 (their Cliopatria shape of 776 covers 603 of the Maitraka core's 637 cells; 32 more lie in the Rashtrakuta shape). OPEN: (a) the Maitraka page says north Gujarat was added under Dharasena III (626-640 on the Vallabhi list) but Cliopatria draws all Gujarat from 476; (b) Toramana's Sanjeli inscription claims Malwa and Gujarat (undated; Toramana defeated 510 and 515) and the Alchon dossier writes a c. 500-515 Hunnic hold on Gujarat, but neither the Toramana nor the Maitraka page mentions the other, so none is drawn; a gap-filler should open the Alchon Huns and Bhatarka pages; (c) the Maitraka page says they 'came under the rule of Harsa in the mid-7th century, but retained local autonomy' and that Dhruvasena II 'married the daughter of Harsavardhana': now recorded here as vassal_start 640 (bridged to Dhruvasena II's accession) and vassal_end 647 (Harsha's death) with counterpart harsha-s-empire; the harsha-s-empire dossier should hold the mirror with counterpart 'maitraka-dynasty' (Harsha's Cliopatria shape covers Ujjain in 612-646 and not in 647-655); (d) the end year differs by page (776, 783) and the Arab invasion is not dated on the Maitraka or Vallabhi pages (the Caliphate page's 723-743 raids did not end the line); (e) Ujjain: the 616 grant shows possession, not conquest; the loss is inferred and was moved from 724 to 732 in the repair pass (the c. 725 date belongs to Nagabhata's Valacha victory, not to Ujjain). STATES NEEDING DOSSIERS: nandipuri-gurjaras (Jayabhata IV, southern Gujarat, 8th century); umayyad-caliphate exists in Cliopatria (656-756). RULERS: the Vallabhi list is the page's, not the Maitraka page's; the Maitraka page names Dharasena II, Dharapatta, Dhruvasena I, Dharasena IV, Siladitya I (Hiuen Tsang visit, 640) with no years; 'Chakravarti Raja Ghana Sen IV' on the list is the Dharasena IV of the prose by reading. GAZETTEER: none missing; Vallabhi (Vala) is not a gazetteer place, so the capital is a coordinate. REPAIR PASS 2026-10-19 (after review): (1) vassal_start 640 / vassal_end 647 with harsha-s-empire added (Maitraka, Harsha and Vallabhi pages reopened); (2) /ledger 555 counterpart changed from vakataka-kingdom to kalachuris-of-mahishmati (the vakataka-kingdom dossier ends in 510 and hands the Gujarat edge to the Kalachuris; no dossier for them yet); (3) the Ujjain loss moved from 724 to 732 to meet Cliopatria's Gurjara-Pratihara row and Nagabhata I's reign start (Caliphate page reopened: the c. 725 date is for the Valacha victory, 'no authentic information about where precisely'); new keyframe 732-776 and the 724 keyframe now holds Ujjain through 731; (4) the 616 note records that Cliopatria's Harsha shape covers Ujjain 612-646; (5) the 476 keyframe now holds 476-533 (verdict ok) and a one-year keyframe maitraka-dynasty_475 draws Saurashtra alone in the founding year.
